strategy.summary: Drehteile Fuchsreiter is a small founder-owned turning shop (18 staff, turnover under EUR 2M, thin equity, stable credit index, VDA 6.3 grade A). It wants work: it advertises free capacity, the second shift has been on hold since spring and it has paused hiring. It also wants cash: it complained about our overdue invoices and offered a cash discount for payment within 10 days. It supplies part:320090 (spacer sleeve) on a 50/50 split with Ilzauer and charges slightly more than Ilzauer. We own the tooling. It is qualified on part:320060 with a 0% quota (Lindlbauer is cheaper) and is invited to the HX shaft RFQ (part:320070). Leverage is ours. Its quality is better than both rivals, its delivery reliability has slipped, and our chronic late payment is its legitimate grievance. Our best currency is volume and fast, reliable payment, not price pressure. Squeezing a thinly capitalised supplier hard is unwise; its quality makes it worth keeping. Evidence on its margins is thin: no should-cost exists for 320060 or 320090.
strategy.decision_maker: Most likely the founder/managing director, with little approval ladder. Our contact so far has been sales only, so this is unconfirmed.

persona.style: Pragmatic, cooperative small shop. It settles below its own ask and voices grievances (late payment) politely but with a hint of consequences.

better ppm than both rivals on comparable parts

needs.detail: Second shift idle, hiring paused, publicly seeking customers. A larger quota on 320090, a share of 320060 or the HX shaft award are its biggest prizes.
Asks for payment on time and offers a cash discount for 10-day payment. Our record shows most invoices paid late.
Calls Hollerau an important reference customer.
Values binding volume and a longer commitment, as a small shop with idle machines.

constraints.detail: Thin equity and small turnover. Our late payment hurts it.
320090 prices are fixed per calendar year, with changes requiring 90 days' notice before year end. The term auto-extends unless we give notice, so our exit remains open.
Cost drivers are genuinely up: cold-drawn bars sharply higher year on year, the 1.4404 alloy surcharge and labour moderately higher. A further cut on 320090 lacks a cost basis.
Delivery reliability has slipped below the contractual target. Extra volume may strain it unless the second shift restarts.

Anchors the HX shaft quote near full cost plus a fair margin.
Growing hub volume makes a second-source share attractive.

Bars falling from their peak; this part has the highest bar weight.
Power cost is down; a small, fresh filler argument.
Delivery is below target. A late filler only; partly caused by our rush orders.
The price is fixed per year and needs timely notice; use if it requests a mid-year change.

trades.why: It is short of cash and offers a discount itself. Give shorter payment in the last round for a price step, or at least commit to paying on time.
Idle capacity: a binding volume or a quota shift on 320090, or a share of 320060/320070, is worth more to it than it costs us. Commit only within our need.
Planning security for a small shop. Offer 24 months as a trade; 36 adds nothing.
Only if it insists. Bars are volatile but past their peak, so a clause with no deadband could beat a fixed-price uplift.
Its standard lead time works. With spare capacity, lead time is not a constraint; do not pay for shorter.
Its quality is already good. Keep current targets rather than spend price on them.

price_view.reasoning: On 320090 it is barely above the rival and its cost drivers rose, so the goal is to hold the price or concede at most a small part of any increase. Its history suggests asks for increases do not survive. On 320060 its quote sits well above the incumbent, so there is sizeable room if it wants the share. On the HX shaft, the should-cost plus a fair margin sets the target. Room comes from trading volume and payment, not from cost arguments.

do: Acknowledge our late payments openly and commit to improving
Recognise its quality record and its reference-customer relationship
Frame offers as partnership: more work and reliable cash in return for a sharp price
Answer every message with a term sheet
dont: Do not threaten to move quota or terminate
Do not ask open questions about its cost structure
Do not ask for long payment terms
Do not issue deadlines or ultimatums

traps: Asking for longer payment terms ignores its explicit cash need and its complaint; it would read as not listening
Using delivery reliability as a main lever invites a counter about our rush orders and late payment
Threatening to shift volume to Ilzauer lacks credibility, since Ilzauer's quality on this part is worse
Citing rival prices the case does not list costs trust and reveals rival data
Citing peak-based index figures that are not checkable, or market news not about this supplier
Pressing below its full cost risks a thin-equity supplier we want to keep
Giving shorter payment mid-negotiation lets it be absorbed into a normal step; hold it for the final round
Countering below a declared final offer
strategy.writer_notes: Lead with what it needs: work and cash. Pair every price ask with a volume prospect (quota on the spacer sleeve, a share of the coupling hub, the HX shaft) or with a payment commitment. Admit our late payment once and promise on-time payment; offer faster payment as a closing trade. Praise its quality. Bring one fresh, verifiable record per round. Keep the tone friendly and personal for a founder-run shop.
questions_to_ask: Would added volume from us let you restart your second shift, and how would that affect your pricing?
What cash discount would you grant for payment within your proposed short period?
Which terms (contract length, binding volume, payment) matter most to you in this round?
What lead time could you commit to if you took on additional parts?

findings.text: Part 320060 (coupling hub): Fuchsreiter is not the incumbent (Lindlbauer holds 100% quota). Its new quote of EUR 17.87 is +3.3% on its own 2025 quote of 17.30 and +9.6% above what we pay Lindlbauer (EUR 16.30, also re-quoted at 16.30 on 2026-09-15). Its drivers for this part add about +4.6% over 12 months (bars +12.3% at 32% weight, labour +2.7% at 34%, power -3.7% at 5%). That roughly covers its own increase, but Lindlbauer held its price flat despite the same drivers. No should-cost exists, so we cannot say how far above cost it sits. The room to a competitive award is about -9%.

Part 320090 (spacer sleeve, 50% quota): its price fell from 5.00 (2023) to 4.64 (2026), -7.2%. The rival Ilzauer is at 4.60, so the gap is only 0.9%. The 12-month drivers point upward, about +3.9% (bars +2.33%, alloy surcharge +0.89%, labour +0.93%, power -0.19%), so a cost case for a further cut is weak. Expect Fuchsreiter to argue for an increase. Our counter is the 4.64 anchor, the rival at 4.60 and its pattern of settling about 1.3 pp below its ask. Price room is small, roughly 4.60-4.64; the aim is to hold the price rather than gain.

Part 320070 (pump shaft HX, new, RFQ open): we have a should-cost of EUR 36.87 without margin (material 12.91, conversion 16.78, overhead 7.19; error ±10%). With a 8-12% margin, a fair price is about EUR 40-41. Any quote above about EUR 44 would sit far above full cost. There is no price history and no quote yet.

The cold-drawn bar index rose +12.3% year on year, but it has fallen 2.3% since its June 2026 peak and stands 7.5% below its 2022 high. Power is -3.7% over 12 months. The rise therefore looks past its peak, which argues against a full pass-through and in favour of time-limited or index-linked terms.

Economic context: Fuchsreiter has free capacity (second shift on hold) and wants faster payment. We pay late, on average 11 days after due. Offering payment on time or faster is a cheaper concession for us than giving up price. Evidence on its margins is thin: there is no should-cost for 320060 or 320090.

findings.text: Small founder-owned turning shop (18 staff, turnover 0-2 M EUR, equity ratio 19.6%, credit index 228 unchanged for 12 months, VDA 6.3 grade A, ISO 9001). Decisions most likely sit with the founder/owner, with little approval ladder, so trades can be agreed quickly. The finances are thin but stable: no acute distress signal. The evidence on who decides is thin: we only have contact with 'sales'.

Underutilised and hungry for work. It advertised free machine capacity and paused hiring (March 2026). In June and July 2026 it repeated that it can take additional parts at short notice, with the second shift on hold since spring. Volume and new parts (e.g. the pump shaft HX, part:320070, from 2027) are its main need and our strongest currency.

Cash is a pressing need. It complained about overdue invoices and threatened to 'review our conditions' (2026-08-18). It then offered a cash discount for payment within 10 days (2026-09-04). Our record justifies the complaint: 89.9% of invoices paid late, on average 11.1 days after due, max 24 days late, 2 unpaid. Faster or on-time payment is a cheap trade that gives them what they need. Our late payment is also their legitimate grievance and weakens our moral position until we fix it.

It values Hollerau for recognition: it called us an important reference customer (supplier day 2026-08-11). Our spend is about 5.9% of its turnover. Respectful acknowledgement of the partnership and its quality record should land well.

Its position is weak on part:320090. It is 50% dual-sourced against Drehzentrum Ilzauer at EUR 4.60 versus its own EUR 4.64, and we own the tooling. On part:320060 it holds a 0% quota while Lindlbauer supplies at EUR 16.30. Historically it settles below its own ask (3 renewals: asked -1.1%, settled -2.4%).

Its performance is mixed. On-time delivery fell to 88.0% (from 100%), below the 95% target though above the peer median of 84.6%. Quality is good at 318 ppm against a peer median of 457. There were 4 complaints on part:320090, all with closed 8D reports.
It shows operational discipline: it announces the holiday shutdown and asks for call-offs by 10 December. Plan January volumes accordingly.

findings.text: Framework agreement ctr:4600070250 covers only part:320090 (Spacer sleeve): prices fixed per calendar year, changes need written notice 90 days before year end (i.e. by ~2 Oct 2026 for 2027); payment 30 days net (our standard is 60, so this already favours them); EXW, 28-day lead time; quality agreement with 95% OTD target and EUR 150 flat fee per complaint.

Term runs to 2027-06-30 and auto-extends 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice (by 2027-04-01). The exit is still open and credible, but the term (mid-year) and the price clause (calendar year) are misaligned.

History on part:320090: in three renewals they asked -3.9%, +1.3%, -0.8% and settled -5.2%, 0%, -2.1%, so on average 1.3 pp below their ask. The one increase they asked for was settled at zero. Price went from 5.00 (2023) to 4.64 now (-7.2%). Expect them to move; a requested increase has historically not survived.

Dual source on 320090 at 50/50 with Ilzauer (active since 2018), and we own the tooling, so quota can shift. Ilzauer pays 4.60 against Fuchsreiter's 4.64. Benchmark RFQ rfq:6000000114 in 2025 was awarded to Ilzauer.

On part:320060 Fuchsreiter is qualified with 0% quota, and Lindlbauer holds 100% with our tooling. A second-source RFQ (rfq:6000000213) is quoted. It is also invited to the open new-part RFQ for 320070 (HX shaft, SOP 2027-03). These offer new volume we can trade for concessions on 320090.

Dependency is asymmetric in our favour. Our spend is ~EUR 59k/yr, about 5.9% of a small (18 staff, <2M EUR) supplier's turnover. They advertise free capacity, the second shift is on hold, and they call us an important reference customer. Our dependency is low given the dual source on 320090.

Weak spot on our side: we pay 11 days late on average (90% of invoices late), breaching clause 4.1. They have complained and ask for payment in 10 days against a cash discount. Their equity ratio is 19.6%, so cash matters to them. Faster payment is a cheap trade for us.
Performance: OTD fell to 88% against the 95% target in clause 6.1. There were 4 complaints on 320090 with EUR 600 recharged, but ppm improved to 318 and is below the peer median.

findings.text: Fuchsreiter currently supplies only part:320090 (spacer sleeve) to us, on a 50% split with sup:70295 Ilzauer. Both get identical volume (12,500 pcs last 12m). Fuchsreiter charges EUR 4.64 against Ilzauer's 4.60 (+0.9%).

On-time delivery has slid from 100% (2025Q3) to 88% vs requested and 92% vs confirmed (2026Q3). That is below the 95% contract target for the last two quarters' windows, though above the 84.6% peer median. Late lines average 11 days, max 14. Rising lateness while it advertises free capacity is a fair point for us.

Quality is its strong card. Rolling ppm is 318, down from a 496 peak, against a peer median of 457 and Ilzauer's 797 ppm on the same part. There are no overdue 8Ds. It has 12 supplier-caused QNs over 3 years at EUR 150 each, with 4 in the last 12 months. The defects are mixed (dimension, leakage, marking), and some 8D closures took more than 60 days (qn:20004953 took 94 days).

Volume outlook for 320090 is +7.7% (27,000 next 12m vs 25,080 ordered), shared with suppliers. Shifting quota away from Ilzauer, the worse-quality source, is a meaningful volume lever for a firm with turnover under EUR 2M and idle capacity. Forecast snapshots for 320090 swing 2-19% (change_pct), so a binding volume promise carries risk.

New parts give us bundling leverage on a firm with idle capacity:
- part:320070 HX shaft (SOP 2027-03, 2,390 pcs forecast, 1.4404) has no source yet; should-cost is EUR 36.87.
- part:320060 is qualified at Fuchsreiter with a 0% quota. Lindlbauer holds 100% at 16.30 and has 669 ppm.

Price on 320090 has fallen 7.2% since 2023 (5.00 to 4.64), and it habitually settles below its ask. However, its 14 rush lines vs Ilzauer's 11, plus 4 changed lines, show we stress it with short-notice orders.

arguments.text: Our quality is the best in your spacer-sleeve supply base. The last-12-month ppm on 320090 is 318, against 797 at Ilzauer, and we have no overdue 8D reports. Lindlbauer runs at 669 ppm on 320060. Every complaint we avoid saves you more than the 4 cents per piece between us and Ilzauer.

Our input costs have risen while our price has fallen. Cold-drawn bar is up 12.3% year on year, the stainless alloy surcharge is up about 6%, and manufacturing labour is up 2.7%. Over the same period we accepted -5.2%, 0% and -2.1% at the last three renewals, so our price is down 7.2% since 2023. A further cut has no cost basis, and a moderate increase would be justified.

You pay us late. 89.9% of our invoices were paid after the due date, on average 10-11 days late and at worst 24 days. That is effectively a free extension of credit to you. Prompt payment is the condition for us to keep sharpening our price.
We have free capacity right now and can absorb short-notice volume, including your rush orders. That makes us a secure second source for 320060 and a credible supplier for the HX shaft.
Under the contract our price is fixed for the calendar year. Any change needs written notice 90 days before year end, so this is an orderly renewal and not open-ended pressure.

weak_points: Our delivery reliability has slipped to 88% on time, below the 95% target in clause 6.1.
We are 4 cents above Ilzauer on 320090, and we lost the 2025 benchmark RFQ (5.10 against 5.00).
Our 320060 quote of 17.87 is 9.6% above Lindlbauer's 16.30.
We have publicly said we need customers; our second shift is idle and hiring is paused.
We have thin equity and a turnover under EUR 2M, and we need the cash.
The customer owns the tooling, so switching away from us is cheap for them.
Power costs are down 3.7% year on year, and the 1.4404 alloy surcharge is 13% below its peak.
We have had 12 supplier-caused complaints on 320090, even though our ppm is the lowest.
wants: Payment within 10 days, or at least strict 30-day payment, in exchange for a 2% cash discount or a price reduction.
A larger quota on 320090 (for example 60-70%), for which we would hold or slightly cut the price.
A share of part 320060; we could move toward roughly 16.6-17.0 if a quota is bound.
The HX shaft award, priced at should-cost plus a fair margin.
A binding annual volume and a 24-36 month term.
An index clause on stainless bar if the customer insists on a fixed price over several years.
red_lines: No price on 320090 below about 4.55 without both volume and payment improvement.
No further cut without a counter-concession.
No ppm or chargeback commitments that we cannot meet.
No longer payment terms than 30 days.
red_team.opening: Thank you for the partnership. We value Hollerau as a reference customer. Our quality on the spacer sleeve is clearly the best among your suppliers (318 ppm). Our input costs have risen sharply: bar steel is up 12.3% and the stainless surcharge about 6%. We have nevertheless reduced our price three times. For 2027 we propose holding 4.64. In return we ask for reliable 30-day payment, or 10-day payment with a 2% discount. We would also welcome a higher quota and access to 320060 and the HX shaft, where we have immediate free capacity.

rebuttals.answer: We agree your quality is a real strength, and we value it; it is a main reason we want to keep and grow the relationship. Quality is already expected under our quality agreement, and complaints still occur and are charged per case, so it supports keeping your share rather than a price premium. On the coupling hub, quality helps your case for a share, but the gap to the incumbent's price is far larger than any quality saving would cover.

Cold-drawn bar and labour have risen, and we recognise that. Weighted by their share of a spacer sleeve, they support only a modest effect, not the full headline rise. Part of it is offset: bar prices have eased since their recent peak, the alloy surcharge fell back recently and power costs are lower. Your earlier reductions were settled freely, and the second source on the same part, with our tooling, is still slightly below you. That points to holding today's price, not to an increase.

You are right, and we apologise: we have paid too many of your invoices late, and that is not acceptable to us either. We commit to paying on time from now on. We are also willing to discuss your proposal of faster payment against a cash discount, as part of the overall agreement on price.

We welcome your free capacity; it is exactly why we see room for more work together, on the spacer sleeve, the coupling hub and the new pump shaft. Volume is worth more to a shop with idle machines, so we expect it to be reflected in sharp prices. Your recent on-time delivery has fallen below the agreed target, so we would like to see it recover before adding volume.

Agreed, the contract gives an orderly annual process, and we will follow it. The same contract fixes today's price as the starting point and runs on unless either side gives notice, so both of us keep options. We prefer to use the renewal to agree a longer, fair arrangement.

press: We would welcome your plan to bring on-time delivery back to the agreed target, especially if we add volume.
On the spacer sleeve, the second source with our tooling is currently slightly below your price, so we would ask you to match it rather than move away from it.
For the coupling hub, your quote is well above what we pay today, so we would need a much sharper price to give you a share.
In past renewals we have always found a fair settlement below the opening ask, and we hope to do the same this time.
Power costs and the alloy surcharge have eased recently, which we hope you can take into account.
